newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises again as Q4, gas year 1997 busiest.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises again as Q4, gas year 1997 busiest.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices continued their upward trend on Monday, traders and brokers said, with interest concentrated on the fourth quarter 1997 and in the gas year starting in October.
The gas year has been busy in recent days and has climbed consistently from the low 12's a therm to its current level above 13.00 pence.
"It's drifting up as there are more buyers than sellers," said a trader. "The gas year has been relatively low and is coming up to a more normal level."
He said the "true" range for the gas year should be between 12.00 pence and 14.00 pence a therm, so the current valuation at a little over 13.00 pence is appropriate.
Another was less convinced, saying that "over 13 pence we'd expect to see a few more sellers," and this could put the year under pressure again.
A seller at St Fergus reported receiving a bid at 12.525 pence a therm for the gas year, although no trade was done.

"But the fact that St Fergus was bid at 12.525 certainly indicates that 13.15 (at the NBP) is do-able," he said. By the close the NBP gas year was bid at 13.05 pence and offered at 13.15 pence, a broker said.

The day ahead was reported twice at 9.45 pence a therm for a total of 200,000 therms. And there were three trades reported from the summer of 1998, but otherwise all reported trade covered either the gas year or the coming winter.
But one trader said there was no particular factor behind this. "It's the middle of summer and everyone's just trading on sentiment," he said.
The IPE saw its recent pick up in activity continue as 250 lots were traded, all in the period November to February, and mostly at higher prices.
The prices of individual months on the IPE corresponded closely to values on the OTC market, dealers said.
